title: Rare Rain Brings Bright Flowers to Chile’s Atacama Desert
summary:
Bright wildflowers are growing across Chile’s Atacama Desert after rare rain. The rain is linked to this year’s very strong El Niño. A report published on October 2, 2026, describes flowers spreading across hills and flat land in one of Earth’s driest places.

The rain helped millions of seeds and bulbs start growing. Bulbs are plant parts that grow underground. Seeds and bulbs can rest underground for years until enough water arrives. Land that usually has few plants is now covered with purple, pink, white, red and yellow flowers.

In Chile, people call this event “desierto florido.” This means “flowering desert.” Jorge Carabantes leads the Protected Areas Department at Chile’s National Forest Corp., also called CONAF. He told The Associated Press that more than 200 plant species, or kinds of plants, are part of the bloom. He said this desert flowering is unusual and different from blooms elsewhere.

The Atacama usually gets only 0.6 inches, or 15 millimeters, of rain each year. Between July and August 2026, several regions in Chile had record rainfall. Carabantes said some areas got more than 190 millimeters. Some regions had not seen that much rain since the 1950s. These numbers describe several Chilean regions. They are not one rain measurement for the whole desert.

The flowers cover about 6,560 square miles, or 17,000 square kilometers. CONAF representatives told The Associated Press that this is the Atacama’s largest bloom since 1997.

Tourists and photographers have come to see the flowers against the mountains. Photos show cacti among the flowers and purple flowers across the flat land.

The flowers will not stay all year. Many will disappear by the end of spring in the Southern Hemisphere, the southern half of Earth. They will leave seeds and bulbs underground. These can wait for another time when unusually heavy rain arrives.
why_it_matters: The bloom shows how rain can change a very dry place and help plants that have waited underground for years begin growing.
